statement: A car ferry has deck space for the equivalent of $40$ cars. The inequality $c + 3t \le 40$ describes the numbers of cars, $c$, and trucks, $t$, that the ferry can carry on one trip. What is the best interpretation of the number $3$ in this context?

choices.text: The ferry can carry at most $3$ trucks on one trip.
choices.misconception: I read the 3 as a limit on the number of trucks, but it multiplies $t$, so it describes how much space each truck uses.

choices.text: Each truck takes up as much deck space as $3$ cars.
The ferry carries $3$ more trucks than cars on every trip.
choices.misconception: I thought the 3 compared the numbers of trucks and cars, but it is a coefficient on $t$, not an amount added to $c$.

choices.text: Each car takes up as much deck space as $3$ trucks.
choices.misconception: I reversed the comparison: the 3 is attached to $t$, so it is each truck that counts as 3 cars, not each car that counts as 3 trucks.

hints: The left side measures deck space in units of one car.
Ask how much the left side grows when one more car boards, and how much it grows when one more truck boards.
One more car adds $1$ to $c + 3t$, and one more truck adds $3$. Compare those two amounts of space.

solutions.reliable: The expression $c + 3t$ counts deck space in car-sized units: each car adds $1$ unit and each truck adds $3$ units, and the total can be at most $40$ units. So the coefficient $3$ means that one truck uses the same deck space as $3$ cars. For example, $10$ trucks and $10$ cars use $10(3) + 10 = 40$ units, a full deck. Key idea: in a constraint like $c + 3t \le 40$, each coefficient is the amount of the shared resource used by one unit of that variable.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
